summary: Georges Dumézil was a scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the University of Paris under Antoine Meillet and Marcel Mauss, later holding posts at Istanbul University, the EPHE, and the Collège de France.
Georges Guieysse was an Indologist and linguist. Between circa 1886 and 1889, he studied under Sylvain Lévi, Michel Bréal, Abel Bergaigne, Ferdinand de Saussure, and James Darmesteter.

Georges Perrot was a French archaeologist and historian. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure in 1852, he held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the University of Paris, and served as director of the École Normale Supérieure.

Georges Redard was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Neuchâtel, Bern, Paris under Émile Benveniste, and Tehran, later holding professorships at the University of Bern and the University of Lausanne.

Georges Strehly was an Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, the Sorbonne, and the EPHE under Paul Regnaud and Abel Bergaigne. He held teaching posts at Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1879–1886) and Lycée Louis-le-Grand (1886–1906).

Georges-Jean Pinault is a linguist and specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at the ENS, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE under Jean Haudry, later holding professorships at Blaise Pascal University and the EPHE.

Georgij Aleksandrovič Zograf was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov and Vasilij Matveevič Beskrovnyj, later serving as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Georgij Saridanovič Ahvlediani was a linguist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Kharkiv and Saint Petersburg under Friedrich Knauer, Carl Salemann, and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy, later becoming a professor at Tbilisi State University and head of division at the Institute of Linguistics.
Georgios Kozakis Typaldos worked in Indology and studied medicine at the University of Padua. He served as librarian at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens from circa 1845 to 1863.

Georgios Nikolaou Hatzidakis was a linguist who studied at Athens, Leipzig, Jena, and Berlin under scholars including Windisch, Curtius, Brugmann, Delbrück, and Schmidt. He served as rector of Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and president of the Academy of Athens.

Georgios T. Halkias is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble, later becoming the Glorious Sun Endowed Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong.

Gerald B. Kelley was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1955. He taught at Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1957 to 1963 before becoming a professor at Cornell University in 1963.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig (1969–1974). He held posts at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine (1979–1989), the University of Göttingen (circa 1994–2016), and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen (circa 2004–2016).

Gerald James Larson specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. After studying at Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University, and under Ram Shankar Bhattacharya, he was a professor of religious studies at UC Santa Barbara and Indiana University Bloomington.

Gerald Patrick Moriarty was an English historian and Indologist. Educated at Balliol and Pembroke Colleges, Oxford, he served as an Oxford tutor, a member of the Indian Civil Service, and Cambridge's University Teacher of Indian History (1897–1924).

Gerald Schwedler is a historian who studied in Salzburg, Oxford, Rome, and at Heidelberg University. He has held positions at the University of Zurich, University of Konstanz, Heidelberg University, and was appointed to a chair at Kiel University in 2018.
Gerard Abraham Joseph was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who was a member of the Ceylon Civil Service. In 1893, he became the secretary and librarian of the National Museum of Colombo.

Gerard Leslie Makins Clauson was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eton College and Corpus Christi College, Oxford, and later held a post at the University of Oxford.

Gerardus van der Leeuw was a Dutch scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University from circa 1908 to 1916 and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

Gerasim Stepanovich Lebedev was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Das in 1787. He later worked as an interpreter for the Collegium of Foreign Affairs and at the Département asiatique.
